title: Token-latency-driven hiring priority mapping playbook
content:
Purpose:
This notebook ties token-latency SLOs to hiring priority and budget phasing. It is intended for finance + platform partnerships to operationalize when to accelerate hires (infra / serving) vs. when to lean on price changes, autoscale credit, or burst contracts.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
As usage increases, the marginal cost of preserving <100ms tail latency grows nonlinearly when requests exceed sustained dedicated capacity. We propose a three-trigger framework (utilization, tail-latency drift, price elasticity) that maps to hiring actions (immediate hire, staged contractor, postpone). This reduces reactionary hiring and makes pricing-change decisions explicit.

Key definitions and assumptions:
- Baseline hosted API unit economics: revenue per 1k input+output tokens = $0.30 (base). 
- Marginal GPU cost per 1M tokens served (current mix): $110 (includes infra, ops, amortized HW).
- Latency SLO tiers: Gold (p95 < 100ms), Silver (p95 < 250ms), Bronze (p95 < 600ms).
- Typical request token distribution: median tokens/request = 120, 90th pct = 520.
- Hiring cost assumptions: Senior Infra SWE fully loaded annual cost = $350k; Mid SWE = $220k; Contractor equivalent month cost = $25k.
- Lead time to impact: Hiring SWE -> meaningful throughput/latency improvement = 12 weeks; contractor -> 4 weeks (short-term wins); infra purchases (GPUs) procurement lead = 6–10 weeks.

Three-trigger framework (what to watch):
1) Sustained utilization trigger: sustained avg GPU pool utilization > 72% for 7 days over rolling 30-day window.
   - Rationale: headroom for burst and qps variations shrinks; batching/kv-caching techniques have limited additional gains beyond this point.
2) Tail-latency drift trigger: p95 latency increases > 20% vs baseline for > 24 hours and correlates with request growth (not model change).
   - Rationale: indicates queuing/backpressure effects not solved by scheduling/prefetch.
3) Price elasticity trigger: revenue drop (QoQ) relative to tokens served > 6% when price increases of 5% are simulated on top of base offering (indicative of sensitivity).
   - Rationale: if pricing changes materially impact demand, price levers are viable to control load and preserve unit economics.

Action matrix (maps triggers to actions and timing):
- Trigger: Sustained utilization only -> Action: Queue small infra burst (2–4 GPUs), enable temporary burst capacity policy; Defer hire for 8 weeks.
  - Rationale and cost: 4 A100-equivalent GPUs burst @ $18k/month (spot+contracted) = ~$72k/month incremental cost vs hiring a mid SWE (~$18k/mo fully loaded) but provides immediate capacity.
- Trigger: Tail-latency drift (+ utilization) -> Action: Raise hiring priority to P0 for infra SWE, open 2 mid-SWE reqs and 1 contractor; re-evaluate after 12 weeks.
  - Cost estimate: 2 mid-SWE hires = $440k/year; 1 contractor for 3 months = $75k.
- Trigger: Price elasticity high and utilization moderate -> Action: Pilot a small price uplift (3–7%) for new signups/overage buckets, communicate performance improvement; measure 30-day net impact.

Headcount phasing scenarios (12-month forecasts)
Note: scenarios assume current ARR baseline and linear token growth per quarter. All $ in USD.

Scenario A — Conservative growth (token growth +20% QoQ):
- Month 0: baseline infra + 3 infra SWE, 4 platform SRE, 2 infra contractors (telco), capex reserved capacity 40 GPUs.
- Month 3: sustained util >72% -> deploy 8-GPU burst, contractor extension 3 months.  
- Month 6: tail-latency triggers -> hire 1 mid SWE (start), convert 1 contractor -> perm.
- Total incremental headcount by month 12: +2 perm hires, contractor cadence reduced.
- 12-month budget impact: incremental labor ~$440k, burst infra spend (averaged) ~$180k, net margin delta -6.2%.

Scenario B — Aggressive growth (token growth +40% QoQ):
- Month 0: baseline plus 4 infra SWE, 6 SREs, reserved capacity 60 GPUs.
- Month 1-2: utilization triggers immediately -> implement burst + accelerate hiring pipeline.
- Month 3: hires onboard -> additional infra purchase order (24 GPUs) delivered month 8.
- Total incremental headcount by month 12: +6 perm hires, +$420k contractor spend.
- 12-month budget impact: incremental labor ~$1.8M, capex burn $1.1M, price-to-margin pressure unless price increased or efficiency improves.

Scenario C — Price mitigation first (optimize pricing before hires):
- Apply 5% price uplift to overage and high-throughput customers with a 14-day notice window; simultaneously enable advanced batching and KV cache profiles for affected tiers.
- Expected short-term token demand reduction 8–11% (modeled).
- Hiring deferred for 3 quarters; marginal infra spend lower but risk of churn for price-sensitive customers.
- 12-month budget: lower headcount hires (+1 hire), incremental revenue +3% net of churn.

Quick sensitivity model (table, simplified):
Columns: Scenario | Price change | Token change | Revenue delta | Net margin delta | HC hires avoided
- Conservative | +0% | +20% | +18% | -6.2% | 2
- Aggressive | +0% | +40% | +60% | -18.4% | 6
- Price-mitigate | +5% | -9% | +3% | +1.1% | 5 avoided over 12 months

Simple decision heuristics for finance (short checklist):
- If utilization trigger + tail-latency and backlog of 3+ hiring candidates -> approve immediate contractor (up to 3 months) + open 2 perm reqs.
- If only utilization and price elasticity low (<3%) -> prefer burst infra; reassess after 6 weeks.
- If price elasticity high (>8%) -> prioritize price experiment + segmented rollout; only hire if elasticity experiment fails to restore margin.

Operational runbook snippets (how to act quickly):
- Day 0 (signal): Product alerts page and finance dashboard auto-email to list (Finance Ops, Platform Eng EM, Head of Serving Runtime).
- Day 1–7: Enable burst pool (ops playbook id: RB-BURST-02), run model-variant fallbacks for non-critical traffic, notify top-tier customers.
- Week 2–4: If tail-latency persists -> approve contractor spend (up to $75k/month) and start recruitment funnel.
- Week 8–12: Review improvement; if <15% latency improvement, proceed to full hires and capex order.

Sample calculations (worked example):
- Baseline tokens/month = 1.2B tokens. Growth +30% QoQ -> Q2 = 1.56B, Q3 = 2.028B.
- Marginal cost baseline = $110 per 1M tokens -> monthly marginal cost at 1.2B = $132k. At 2.028B -> $223k.
- If to keep Gold SLO we need 20% more GPUs: capex operationalized as 40 extra GPUs at effective monthly cost (amortized + cloud) = $360k/month. Hiring 4 infra SWE (annual fully loaded $350k each) -> monthly cost = ~$116.7k.
- Quick trade: 40 GPUs vs 4 hires over first 6 months: GPUs = $2.16M; hires (6 months cost) = $700k. If hires deliver 35% efficiency (lower capex need), blended cost = $1.54M -> net saving $620k.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Price uplift induces churn among key enterprise customers -> Mitigation: use targeted segmentation, grandfather contracts, short A/B window, include performance improvements in comms.
- Risk: Contractor knowledge drain -> Mitigation: mandate transfer docs, pair contractors with perm engineers, set delivery OKRs.
- Risk: Procurement delays for GPUs -> Mitigation: maintain 2-month safety buffer in capacity planning and pre-book vendor holdback.

Next steps (action items):
- Finance: sign off on contractor budget cap $225k for immediate runway (Elena) by EOD Friday.
- Platform Eng: produce 2-week burst cost estimate for 4/8/16 GPU options with vendor pricing (Marcus) by next Tue.
- Talent: expedite two infra SWE requisitions + shortlist contractors (Priya) by next sprint planning.
- Product: prepare segmented price uplift messaging and experiment plan (Diego) by next Fri.

Appendix: short model pseudocode (how sensitivity run is computed)
- inputs: base_price_per_1k, token_volume_forecast_by_segment, elasticity_by_segment, marginal_cost_per_1M, hiring_costs, capex_profiles
- process: simulate price uplift -> compute token_volume_delta = token_volume_forecast_by_segment * elasticity_by_segment * price_delta; recompute revenue and marginal costs; compute hires required by mapping p95 drift to headcount via historical delta (0.2 hires per 10% sustained p95 drift)
- outputs: revenue_by_scenario, hires_by_scenario, capex_spend_by_scenario

Notes and open questions:
- Need better segment-level elasticity inputs; current numbers use coarse enterprise vs self-serve buckets. Recommend running small price experiments to get empirical elasticity per cohort.
- We should instrument a p95-by-model-by-customer metric to better attribute latency drivers to model choice vs infra saturation.
- How to treat OSS customers and research credits in price experiments? propose exempting for 30 days.

Document history: created 2026-09-12 by Elena Park; reviewed by Finance and Platform on 2026-10-20; updated 2026-11-03 with contractor caps and refined trigger thresholds.
